newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian PM Hun Sen leaves for Burma visit.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian PM Hun Sen leaves for Burma visit.

text.p: Cambodian Second Prime Minister Hun Sen on Tuesday flew to Burma for a four-day official visit during which the two sides are expected to discuss their bids to join ASEAN.
"I think this is an important visit to extend the friendship, understanding and cooperation," Hun Sen told reporters before departing with a delegation of about 30 officials.
The prime minister, who will meet Burmese military leader General Than Shwe and other top officials, said the two sides would sign a cultural agreement and might sign a tourism pact.
Analysts also expected them to discuss their bids to become full members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).
The organisation groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam, while observers Cambodia, Laos and Burma hope to join in July.
Hun Sen said he would stop in Bangkok on Friday for talks with Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh on a range off issues, including security and trade along their common border.
The Cambodian leader is returning a controversial visit by Than Shwe and other military leaders of Burma's State Law and Order Restoration Council in October.

The government called that visit a success despite a street demonstration led by opposition leader Sam Rainsy in support of Burmese democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi on the morning of Than Shwe's arrival in the Cambodian capital.
The two countries agreed during the visit to establish direct air links between their capitals and to open tourism offices in each nation, but no action has been taken yet.
